newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr moves narrowly vs yen, down vs mark in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr moves narrowly vs yen, down vs mark in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar hovering narrowly versus yen in morning Tokyo after earlier easing, with support seen near 117.50 yen for now with bids from trust banks and importers, dealers said.
*Overseas operators said to be keen to sell dollars just below 118 yen to avoid hitting options positions, which is weighing on dollar/yen.
*Dollar down vs mark due to profit-taking and mark's rise against yen, dealers added.
*Options-related dollar sales to avoid hitting knock-out positions at around 1.85 marks expected to emerge on dollar's rises against mark, a dealer at a long-term credit bank said.
*A trust bank dealer said some investment trust firms and trust banks were eager to buy marks for yen to unwind hedge mark sales as dollar/yen also maintains bullish tone.
*Mark stood near 64.03/06 yen at 0133 GMT, compared with 63.91 yen in early Tokyo trade.
*The long-term credit bank dealer said market becoming more nervous about possible comments by German officials to talk up mark, prompting dollar/mark profit-taking sales.

*Dollar eased slightly against yen in early Tokyo trade partly due to comments by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky that U.S. automotive trade deficit with Japan is getting worse and that Tokyo has fallen short of fulfilling agreement to open its market.
*Profit-taking weighed on dollar after it failed to break above 200-day moving average of 117.97 yen overnight, which is widely seen as key resistance point.
*Talk of sales of dollars for yen by Asian central banks.
*"There is no question that Japan has stalled on deregulation in (the auto) sector. That is of significant concern and inexcusable," Barshefsky told Reuters in an interview on Monday.
*Dollar continued to gain against sterling in Tokyo after British pound fell sharply overnight versus mark.
*Sterling tumbled about five pfennigs in New York on Monday on profit-taking and speculation that U.K. interest rates may remain steady in near term.
*Sterling's weakness against mark is likely to indirectly help cap dollar's upside against German currency, traders said.
